answer:
## Headline

**R1 (primary): 18 of 18 = 1.000 (100%)** of the original `ee` (Experimental Economics) studies are coded `online.o == 0` — original data not collected online.

Stated as an assumption, not documentation: no column in either file records "lab setting"; `online.o` is the only field encoding mode of collection, so R1 operationalises *lab* as *not-online*. Because `online.o` has **zero variance** inside `ee` (all 18 == 0), R1 restates a **degenerate distribution**, not a sample proportion. I deliberately report **no confidence interval** — a CI over n=18 on a constant would dress a degenerate distribution as an estimate. The residual uncertainty is definitional and coverage-related, not sampling-related.

## Sensitivity, side by side

| rule | definition | num | den | prop | ids differing vs R1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R1 (primary)** | `online.o == 0` | 18 | 18 | **1.000** | (none) |
| R2 | `online.o == 0 AND subjects.o == 'students'` | 17 | 18 | 0.944 | **ee.4** |
| R3 | `online.o == 0 AND online.r == 0` | 18 | 18 | 1.000 | (none) |

The 18/18→17/18 hinge is surfaced, not buried: **ee.4 "Participation"** — `online.o=0`, `subjects.o='community'`, `compensation.o='cash'`, US → in person (passes R1) but a community rather than student pool (fails R2) = 5.6 pp. R3 ≡ R1 exactly (`online.r` is 0 for all 18).

## R4 — isolated as instructed
`us_lab.o == 1` selects 11/18 = 61.1%, but it is **not an estimate about setting**: (1) `us_lab.o == (experiment_country.o == 'United States')` on **926/926** rows, zero disagreements; (2) **40** rows have `online.o == 1` yet `us_lab.o == 1`. It measures "run in the US". It lives only in section 4 of the report and in NOTES.md — absent from the rules table and the submitted hypothesis. I verified this programmatically (token scan of the hypothesis block: `us_lab`, `61.1`, `11/18`, `926` all absent; section 4 retains the evidence).

## File 2 cross-check — count and scope only
**18 = 18** (`file2 'Experimental Economics'` ↔ `file1 'ee'`; vocabularies differ, codes not interchangeable). Full auditable 18-row match table printed (lead surname + year + venue; year 18/18, venue 18/18). File 2 has **no setting columns** (keyword scan → NONE). Its one duplicate label (`P Bressan, D Stranieri`) is in Psychology, outside `ee`.

`n.o` vs `no` agree 6/18; `p_value.o` vs `po` 15/18 → the files count different quantities. Reported as a reason they are **not interchangeable**, not as evidence about setting; it moves the estimate in neither direction.

## Two self-corrections I want on the record
1. **I overclaimed the `Fehr`/`pub_year` role.** My first run printed that year-matching resolved the Fehr collision. Testing the variants showed the *selected* heuristic (lead surname, last token) needs **no** year disambiguation — 0/18 rows — because restricting to the **lead** surname already removes the collision; that collision belongs to the *variant* that matches against *any* author surname. I patched the script to print a 3-variant table and state this explicitly.
2. **My first hypothesis draft named `us_lab`,** violating your separation rule. Removed and verified by token scan.

## Caveats in the deliverable
C1 definitional (rule choice drives 100% vs 94.4%); C2 zero-variance/no interval; C3 coverage (`lab_id` 0/18, `us_lab.*` unusable); C4 **denominator provenance, labelled external** — 18 rows is the denominator actually present, published EERP accounts describe a larger candidate set, and no external count was imported nor any external per-study lab verification performed; C5 scope = hypothesis about these files. `discipline == 'Economics'` reported as coextensive (18 rows, 0 outside `ee`) and **not** used as a second selector.

Supporting internal contrast, same dataset: `ee` 0/18 originals online vs `ml1` 37/592 (6.2%).

**Artifacts:** `analysis/ee_lab_setting.py` (346 lines, compiles, byte-identical across two runs), `analysis/ee_lab_setting_output.txt` (231 lines), `analysis/NOTES.md`.

payload.hypothesis: Essentially all Experimental Economics studies in this dataset were conducted in a lab (in-person) setting: 18 of 18 (100%) of the original ee studies are coded online.o == 0, with all 18 also in-person on the replication side and all paid in cash; under a stricter definition requiring a student subject pool it is 17 of 18 (94.4%), the sole exception being ee.4 'Participation' (community pool). So the proportion is 1.00 under the primary definition and no lower than about 0.94 under the stricter one. This rests on a modelling assumption, since neither file records a 'lab setting' variable and lab_id is empty for all 18 rows, and because online.o has zero variance within ee the figure restates a degenerate distribution rather than a sampled proportion, so it carries definitional rather than sampling uncertainty. Within these files ee is distinctly in-person (0/18 online vs 37/592 in Many Labs 1), though 'not online' cannot by itself separate a physical lab from another in-person venue, and the estimate covers the 18 replicated pairs present here rather than any wider candidate list.
payload.workflow: Read-only profiling of project labels and the ee subset (18 O/R pairs = 18 distinct original studies; aggregated all NaN, drop all False, 0 duplicates) -> inventory of every candidate setting proxy reporting coverage AND variance, which showed online.o/online.r/same_online/subjects.r/compensation.* are constant within ee and lab_id is 0/18 populated -> verified two schema-vs-data contradictions before writing any rule (same_online encodes 'same online status', 732/732; us_lab.* is a US-location dummy, 926/926 agreement with country=='United States' plus 40 online studies flagged us_lab==1) -> applied R1 (online.o==0, primary), R2 (+subjects.o=='students'), R3 (+online.r==0) over the 18 original studies with per-study assignment, plus R4 kept strictly inside a rejected-proxy section -> scoped file-2 cross-check as count-and-scope only (18=18, auditable lead-surname+year+venue match table, three variant-labelled failure modes), explicitly excluding file2 n/p columns from inference because the files count different quantities (6/18 and 15/18 agreement).

rejected_proxy_reported_separately.status: invalid proxy (US-location dummy), excluded from headline and hypothesis text

payload.no_confidence_interval_rationale: online.o has zero variance within ee; a CI over n=18 on a constant would misrepresent a degenerate distribution as a sampled estimate
